Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies, authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for feedback on a full draft.

Please first go to the Ideas forum and read the required forum guidelines, or go to the chat and give a quick summary of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you ensure that the premise is something that will be successful with the community audience.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Tower of Babel (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Occurs over several iterations, with the threat increasing over time

+ View Block
- Hide

Elevator Pitch: - A memetic effect which can be transferred through print, speech, or digital media.

-The infection causes all infected individuals to begin speaking in an info-hazardous language. Every 2 days infected individuals will become paralysed for an increasing period of time. Within 7 months this paralysis will become permanent.

-Individuals affected by the anomaly will be conscious during the period of paralysis, being somehow disconnected from their body and walking around in an incorporeal form. Within this form, they will be unable to communicate with any other affected individuals or non-affected individuals. When in this form, a massive black obelisk, which called Iskententhine (translating to 'That which is the end)

-Affected individuals are unaware of the memetic basis of their infection unless told, and as such are likely to speak to everyone as if speaking in normal English.

Central Narrative: -Anomaly is first thought to be safe, as an anomaly affecting the population of a factory near a city that doesn't exist (this is important), but soon is reclassified as Euclid as several foundation researchers and D-Class are infected (The Euclid level object is a new iteration). The foundation researchers are amneticised [[footnote]] This is spelled wrong]] and contained, but it is believed that one infection gets out, as the infection reappears in the high school where a researchers son lives.

-Object is re-classified as Keter after the infection is thought to be neutralised by aggressive foundation action, and efforts to bury all affected individuals. The effect re-appears in several different locations following this, and soon large swaths of humanity are infected. Several prominent foundation members move into secure facilities to wait out the disaster. SCP-2000 is activated, the foundation recommends suicide for all individuals and efforts from several Groups of interests create a 1km layer of dirt and dust over the original earth, creating new geological formations. Shortly after, the O5 leave the containment chamber, recreate humanity, and continue.

The final iterations object class is Cernunnos, and it seems that the infection has arisen again, in Site 102, Canberra, Australia.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Will the foundation sacrifice human communication permanently to save humanity?

Notes: I had a wildly different idea under the same name previously. This article is completely different from that (the only thing in common is the hook), so I've put it in a new thread.

item.content:encoded:
Mindlessly uses the wrong spelling of "hole" in post description.

Genre (Optional): Suspense / Horror ?

Elevator Pitch: An area approximately 22 metres and an unknown depth has become intangible (simply put, any person who walks into this area will fall straight through the ground to an unknown depth).

Central Narrative: The Foundation builds a site around this area and begins to study it, sending test subjects down the "invisible hole" to their deaths in futile attempts to find out where it leads.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Unknown to the Foundation until later, every time they've sent a test subject through, a new similar sized area becomes intangible. item.title: Re: SCP Idea looking for greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Summoned by PM:

Hi there Noah J Cooper. Let’s take a look at your concept.

So my initial comment to you (through PM) was that the concept hasn’t been fleshed out fully, and I still stand by that assessment. You should endeavour to use all 400 words of the limit, and it’s a red flag if you haven’t done that: it usually means the concept isn’t able to stand on its two feet.

True to nature, I’m seeing a few issues with the concept, which I will list down below:

(1) When I read your elevator pitch, I don’t really understand the mechanics of how the scp operates. Okay, so it explodes and takes over people. What does it mean to “get access to all of the previous hosts memories” and how does the sphere “regenerate”? More importantly, why does this happen? What is the sphere’s purpose in doing this? All these questions could have been explored further.

(2) Under your “Central Narrative” segment, instead of telling us what could be shown in the logs, tell us explicitly what the story is. How exactly does the Foundation discover the scp and contain it? Do they experiment with the scp? What happens when they do? How does your article end? Give us specifics please.

(3) I don’t understand either what you mean at the end when you say “so in a way, it relies on the foundation to survive.” Perhaps it’s because I don’t understand how the scp functions in the first place, so I couldn’t see how the sphere relies on the Foundation to survive. Doesn’t it regenerate on its own as well? So again, I’m left scratching my head.

If you decide to revise the concept further / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply. Best of luck!

item.title: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is large, dark, quadrupedal aquatic lifeform located somewhere in the Atlantic at a site known as The Ring. SCP can only viewed at night at designated platforms 350m below sea level. Videoing or photographing SCP-XXXX must be avoided as well as viewing it for more than 1 minute continuously, or making direct eye contact.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX was first alerted to the SCP foundation through a field agent located inside of NOAA. NOAA identified a drastic change in salinity in an area roughly 1km2 somewhere in the Atlantic. Field Agents Smith, Jones, Roger, Greeves and Alex investigated the site of this anomalous activity using a SCP ship Horizon. Upon arrival the agents confirmed a change in salinity within the area as well as mutated and aggressive versions of the local fauna and flora. All agents sent to investigate this anomalous area during this initial Expedition, never returned. The last contact with the foundation in the transcript logs ended with the lead agent Smith saying:

"It's in the water, its in my head, its on the boat… send Deep Feeders"
After a considerable loss of life and 3 more expeditions were the foundation able to secure SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: SCP-XXXX is capable Phycological Physical Mutation creating a sub entity of various forms like the Gespenst( wraith). SCP is also capable of salinity conversion, which if left uncheck can cause cataclysmic change in weather, flora/fauna, disrupt oxygen levels.

Additional Notes:Constructive criticism is greatly appreciated.👍

item.content:encoded:
Thanks for your detailed explanation. I've got a better understanding of the myth now, but my question is how you plan on presenting this info? The initial concept hints at a discovery and possible exploration log, but what else? If you can outline briefly for us the various components of the article, that will help us visualise the flow of information better.

I also would personally avoid excessive / explicit references to other SCPs - far more effective to make the reference subtle and allow the readers to make the connection on their own.

You're close to a greenlight, for me at least. I'm impressed by your knowledge of mythology and right now it's more a matter of contextualising and presenting said info into a competent SCP narrative. Best of luck!

I go by JoysticKnight (I imagine you could shorten that to Jsk if it's a little much to type out).

As far as the foundation is concerned, I've seen it's growth over the years with the wealth of it's library and the troves of content people make concerning it. item.title: The Painter (Old Concept)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre (Optional): Horror.

Elevator Pitch: The Painter is a humanoid male with little to no facial features except his eyes, he is able to decide the (horrible and gruesome) fate of any living being by painting it on a canvas, no matter how hard his victims will try they will always meet their fate, this manipulates the world around the victim so that they will meet their fate no matter the cost, his only limitation is that he must know how the victim looks like in order to put them on the canvas and decide their fate. The foundation is unable to take the paintbrush and the canvas of the Painter because his own fate is to keep painting, so any attempt in doing so will be an inevitable failure because a series of events will always happen in order for the SCP to get his tools back.

Central Narrative: The Painter's story is that he is the judge of humanity, he is here to create and manipulate everyone's fate, he decides how and when everyone will experience their final moments and he will not stop until everyone's fate is set.

He was originally found in a cabin in the woods after a few campers reported "A weird man painting me and my friends dying in horrible ways". After a few years all of the campers died exactly how they reported the paintings to look like and that's when the foundation stepped in, they used smoke grenades, thermal vision and a bag to blind the target and capture it but being captured by the foundation was only part of his fate.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article will contain a few victims of the Painter and how they met their grim fate, how the foundation will try and stop the painter from continuing his anomalous activities and the effect he had on the world around him and the foundation by deciding people's fate.

Additional Notes: This is an old idea, my first one actually, I made an old thread about it almost a year ago and I'm trying to revisit the concept and improve it. hopefully I will be able to achieve that, if you decide to visit the old thread and find that you like the original concept more or some ideas from it, just let me know.

item.title: The Infinite Beach (Seeking Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): N/A

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP Article. Name, Classification, Containment procedures, description.

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a beach sixty miles south of Long Beach, California upon which, no matter how long an individual walks across the beach, the water can never be reached. However, the water always appears to be no more than eighty to ninety yards away. The actual anomaly is slightly more interesting than that, as you'll see in the central narrative below.

Central Narrative: Through a series of audio logs between expeditionary personnel and command, as well as autopsy reports, readers will follow teams of research personnel sent to explore SCP-XXXX in hopes to discover more about its anomalous nature. The first expeditionary log reveals that the team suffers a casualty by "dry-drowning" around eight km out, and the others are recovered. Autopsy reveals cause of death to be asphyxia by drowning. The second log reveals that the use of a SCBA allows explorers to venture out substantially farther, reaching close to twenty six kilometers before their oxygen tanks reach half-way empty and they have to turn around. The third log follows a team of researchers more well equipped, with oxygen tanks that should last forty-eight hours. The team reports back around fifty-three km out that there is some form of writing in the sand. Later, they report that they can see what they believe to be a boat in the distance, just off shore, however at the fifty-seven km mark three of the five oxygen tanks simultaneously malfunction. The team turns around, holding their breath unless breathing in through the SCBA, which they take turns using to survive. All team members are recovered, and the writing in the sand is sent to linguists for deciphering. Log four, the final log before SCP-XXXX is deemed unfit for exploration, documents the exploration of four research personnel on board a semi-aquatic vehicle designed to withstand high pressure and impact. They make it twenty-six km before the vehicle begins to flood with water. The team is forced to abandon the vehicle and carry on. At the fifty-seven km mark, the lead researcher calls in that there appears to be a tall, disproportionate figure down near the water, henceforth denoted as SCP-XXXX-1. Before command gets a chance to respond, all personnel experience simultaneous SCBA failures, and the hissing of air and screaming of researchers can be heard just before comm connection is lost. Three of the four corpses are recovered and autopsied, and cause of death is determined to be asphyxia by drowning. The fourth cable comes back severed, and there is blood and a torn shred of clothing on the cable.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A beach that kills people by "dry drowning" them is certainly unique. The test logs will serve as something to actually keep readers interested.

Additional Notes: Researchers in the audio logs are tethered by spools of cable so they can be recovered. All feedback still welcome.

I have attached a draft of an audio log (albeit not a great one, it is still a draft) for posterity

Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Drafts Critique
Forum thread: Any improvements?

It seems like this article isn't going to survive very long, but I'm going to try and point out a thing that, for me, could have been a very easy improvement in the writing style.

show
hide

One of the clearest markers of poor writing in this article, for me at least, was the insufficient use of full stops. Every single paragraph in this article is a single sentence. This means there are a lot of extremely long sentences here, which readers can't keep themselves focused on. Beyond that, it also means that in places where paragraphs are fairly uniform in length, such as the interview, sentences are also very uniform. This, to put it bluntly, is boring. It's a type of repetition, and unconscious repetition is very bad for your writing.

In the future, I'd advise mostly writing paragraphs composed of 2-4 sentences, and varying the length of those sentences in order to not bore your audience.

I hope this piece of advice can help you write better in your next article - good luck!

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) His memory is basically a sliding scale; he remembers most of what he's encountered but he has problems with time (so he could place the events in order but not associate those events with a specific time). He also forgets that he dies; he has no idea that he's an anomaly or that he's only alive a week at a time now. He just has an urgency to get things done as quickly as possible.

2) He's not an agent of any GOI. In fact, it was only someone noting the dates and locations of his blog posts that happened to correlate to some missing people that the Foundation even had a clue he existed. (Given the nature of anomalies, I don't see it as a major stretch that the Foundation tracks when people go missing.) While he could theoretically be a decent operative for a GOI, the limitations on his memories make him more of a liability, and he couldn't be used as a reliable means to eliminate someone as you would need to guarantee that the person would a) pick the pack up, and b) would be the person to encounter the pack.

3) The transformation requires possession of the backpack and takes about three hours. The transformation could theoretically be reversed if the person stopped carrying the backpack after an hour or two; the biological template would then reassert itself. After that, it's too late. When the transformation is complete, he gains some of their skills (but they usually only last through the current incarnation) and the person's biometrics (such as fingerprints) but loses the bulk of their memories.

item.title: Re: How to multi-class instances?
item.content:encoded:
An article with a comparable issue is SCP-4812, which uses the placeholder class "See Below" and specifies in a memorandum.

Personally I don't think it matters all that much, unless your narrative is highly focused on the variance in containment difficulty or whatever. Just consider how much effort goes into containing all the anomalies in-aggregate and then chose the class.

It's up to you but there's no need to make things harder than they are.
